Derek — long-form answers below (summarized in attached spreadsheet and diagram). Attaching: redwood_annotated_dataflow_v1.png, redwood_kms_attestation_202605.pdf, redwood_ssq_answers_helix.xlsx

1) Dataflow & PII segmentation- Incoming requests: PII fields are marked via a classification layer in the request pipeline. Non-PII tokens follow the standard generation path. PII tokens may be pseudonymized at the prompt stage using prefix hashing/tokenization if the customer enables "PII masking".
- KV cache: we maintain per-tenant KV caches with TTLs configurable per deployment. For hosted API customers, default session KV TTL is 24 hours; Dedicated/Private can set to 0 for no persistent KV. Caches are stored encrypted in-memory on GPU nodes and flushed according to the TTL.
- Retention: user-level logs (request metadata, traces) default to 30 days; token-level logs are truncated unless customer opts-in for longer retention for debugging.

2) KMS & key custody- Supported: Redwood-managed keys (default), AWS KMS (customer-managed keys), GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault integrations, and HSM-backed BYOK for enterprise Private deployments.
- Custody model: with customer-managed KMS, the customer controls key rotation and revocation. Redwood submits encrypted envelopes to infrastructure tied to the CMK; Redwood does not store plaintext keys.
- Attestation: attached is our KMS attestation (redwood_kms_attestation_202605.pdf) describing HSM protections, key usage policies, and SOC-2 cross-references. For on-prem/private installs, we can provide an HSM key escrow design and support in-scope inspection.

3) Subprocessors & routing- Subprocessors (short list): GPU providers for dedicated pools, managed logging provider, telemetry vendor for anonymized metrics. Full list and effective dates in the spreadsheet.
- Cross-border: Smart routing policies respect customer region preferences; default behavior keeps inference in the nearest compatible region, but embeddings routing may use additional clouds for latency reasons — these are enumerated per-region in the attachment.

Operational controls we call out in the SSQ answers: RBAC (fine-grained via roles), API token scoping, per-route rate limits, automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants, prefix TTL controls for KV caching, and per-route retention override.

Next step: I uploaded the artifacts to the shared drive and attached local copies here for your review. If any items need deeper evidence (e.g., KMS HSM logs, SOC mapping), let us know and we'll schedule a secure artifact exchange.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
